Every command, argument and option of the `riana` command line, generated from the CLI
itself (`riana <command> --help` prints the same text). List options such as `--iso` take
a single comma/space-separated value. The desktop app (`riana gui`) builds the same
settings from its forms.

## `riana integrate`

Integrate isotopomer abundance over retention time.

Extracts each identified peptide's MS1 isotopomer envelope (m0, m1, …) from the mzML and integrates it around the chromatographic apex. With --sdrf, identifications come from a quantms mzTab (DDA) or DIA-NN report.parquet (DIA) and each run's identity (condition, replicate, labeling time, enrichment) from the SDRF; writes one &lt;run&gt;_riana.txt per run and the riana_manifest.tsv that fit and rollup read.

```
riana integrate [OPTIONS] MZML_PATH ID_PATH
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MZML_PATH` | `DIRECTORY` | Folder containing the mzML file(s). |
| `ID_PATH` | `FILE` | The search-ID file: a Percolator target psms.txt (single-mzML path), or — with --sdrf — the quantms mzTab (DDA) / DIA-NN report.parquet (DIA) covering every run. |

### Options

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--sdrf` | `FILE` | – | SDRF samplesheet (the primary path). Drives identity-keyed intake: id_path is read as an mzTab (DDA) or DIA-NN report.parquet (when the SDRF declares DIA), one &lt;mzml_stem&gt;_riana.txt is written per run with its full identity in the header, and a riana_manifest.tsv is written/updated. Without --sdrf, id_path is a Percolator file (the demoted single-mzML tier). |
| `--experiment-column` | `COL` | – | [--sdrf path] SDRF column whose per-row value becomes each run's `experiment` (e.g. 'characteristics[organism part]'), stratifying a multi-factor sheet into separate experiments. Riana groups fits/rollups on (experiment, condition), so the linear-simple Δk then contrasts conditions WITHIN each experiment (e.g. control-vs-KO within each tissue). A matching 'factor value[...]' column (e.g. 'factor value[organism part]') is left out of the condition label, so labels such as 'control' are the same in every experiment. Default: the SDRF file stem on every run (one experiment). |
| `-s`, `--sample` | `TEXT` | `time0` | Sample name for the Percolator (no-SDRF) path; must end with a number encoding the time point, e.g. time1. Ignored with --sdrf (identity comes from the SDRF). |
| `-i`, `--iso` | `TEXT` | `5` | Isotopomers to integrate. Give a single index N for the m0..mN envelope (default '5' = m0-m5, what the D2O fit consumes). An explicit comma/space list is still accepted for a non-contiguous set (e.g. the o18 '0 6' pair). Pass 'auto' for adaptive N_ISO: per-peptide channels from the IsoSpec init+final envelope (≥1% abundance), extracted at averaged-isotopolog accurate mass, padded to the run-wide max width. |
| `--ria` | `FRAC` | – | Precursor enrichment (RIA max), e.g. 0.06 for 6% v/v D2O. Shapes the final envelope under --iso auto. If omitted, taken from the SDRF characteristics[precursor enrichment], else the 0.06 default; given here, overrides the SDRF. |
| `-o`, `--out` | `PATH` | `.` | Output directory [default: .]. |
| `-q`, `--q_value` | `FDR` | `0.01` | Integrate only PSMs with q-value below this [default: 1e-2]. |
| `--peak-rt` | `TEXT` | `apex` | Window anchor: 'apex' (default: the tallest peak near the identification), 'ms2' (0.9.0 parity), or 'consensus' (median apex over m0..m3; prefer at high D2O). |
| `--integration-half-width` | `MIN|AUTO` | `0.15` | Integration half-width in RT min (default 0.15; dial to your chromatographic peak width), or 'auto' to detect boundaries. |
| `-m`, `--mass_tol` | `PPM` | – | Mass tolerance half-width in ppm (±N ppm). If omitted, taken from the SDRF comment[precursor mass tolerance], else the 10 ppm default. Given here, overrides the SDRF. |
| `-W`, `--workers` | `N` | `1` | Runs to integrate concurrently on the --sdrf path (one mzML in memory per worker; 2-4 suits a many-timepoint time series) [default: 1]. Extraction within a run is serial, so this is the way to use more cores. |
| `--resume` | flag | off | On the --sdrf path, skip runs already integrated in the output's manifest at the current settings (each run's &lt;stem&gt;_riana.txt is written as it finishes, so a crashed run resumes where it stopped). Assumes the same SDRF/mzTab inputs. |

### Advanced integration (tuning dials)

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-r`, `--extraction_half_width`, `--r_time` | `FLOAT` | – | Extraction half-width (RT min, both directions): how much XIC to pull around the PSM. If omitted, derived from --integration-half-width / --peak-rt. (alias: --r_time) |
| `--baseline` | `TEXT` | `none` | In-window baseline subtraction: none (default), noise_floor, snip, asls. |
| `--apex-selection` | `TEXT` | `tallest` | Apex pick rule for apex/consensus: tallest (default) or nearest. |
| `--apex-search-half-width` | `MIN` | `0.25` | Half-width (RT min) bounding the apex search around the PSM/MBR RT prior (default 0.25; 0 = whole extraction). Tighter keeps the apex on the confident RT anchor — relevant for cross-proportion / MBR stability. |
| `-w`, `--write_intensities` | flag | off | Also write the pre-integration intensity trace. |
| `-S`, `--smoothing` | `INTEGER` | – | Savitzky-Golay smoothing window (odd int ≥ 3). |
| `--smoothing-polyorder` | `ORDER` | `2` | Savitzky-Golay polynomial order; only used with --smoothing [default: 2]. |
| `-D`, `--mass_difference` | `FLOAT` | `1.003354835` | Mass difference between isotopomers [default: 1.003354835]. |
| `--ppm-alert` | `PPM` | `20.0` | Per-fraction drift-alert threshold: warn when the median ppm error exceeds this [default: 20]. |
| `--prominence-k` | `K` | `3.0` | Apex-finder strictness — a candidate apex must clear K·1.4826·MAD(trace); higher is stricter. Used by --peak-rt apex/consensus and --integration-half-width auto [default: 3.0]. |
| `--width-rel-height` | `FRAC` | `0.05` | Apex-height fraction at which --integration-half-width auto measures the peak width: 0.05 = 5% of apex (Skyline-classic), 0.5 = FWHM (more stable). Only used with --integration-half-width auto [default: 0.05]. |
| `--apex-n-consensus` | `N` | `4` | Leading isotopomer channels (m0..m{N-1}) the consensus apex pools over. Only used with --peak-rt consensus [default: 4]. |
| `--no-id-check` | flag | off | Disable the intake scan↔precursor guard — the per-run check that the mzTab spectra_ref scans point at the matching precursor m/z in this mzML (catches a wrong mzML↔mzTab pairing / quantms filename-prefix scan-scramble; mass-based, so immune to OpenMS RT alignment). Only disable for a run you know is correctly paired. |
| `--precursor-tol-ppm` | `PPM` | `10.0` | Per-scan precursor-m/z match tolerance (ppm) for the intake scan↔precursor guard [default: 10.0]. Lenient to precursor-refinement drift; a wrong file lands hundreds of ppm off. Ignored with --no-id-check. |

### Match-between-runs (MBR)

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--mbr` | flag | off | Match-between-runs (mzTab/DDA, --sdrf path): transfer a confidently identified precursor into the runs of its (experiment, condition) curve that missed it, recovering points lost to stochastic MS2 sampling. Transferred rows are flagged evidence='mbr'; one with no detectable apex is dropped. No-op on DIA (DIA-NN already propagates). |
| `--mbr-min-donor-runs` | `N` | `2` | MBR donor gate: transfer a precursor only if it is confidently identified in at least N runs of the curve group [default: 2]. |
| `--mbr-donor-q` | `Q` | `0.01` | MBR donor-confidence q-value threshold [default: 0.01]. |
| `--mbr-min-snr` | `SNR` | `4.0` | Drop MBR transfers whose apex SNR (prominence/local-noise) is below this (inf SNR — a sparse MAD=0 trace — also fails). Default 4 (0 = ungated): in testing, ungated transfers hurt the fits, while SNR ≥ 4 improved them without degrading clean curves. |
| `--mbr-min-scans` | `N` | `3` | Drop MBR transfers with fewer than N nonzero scans in the integration window (a sparse XIC can't define a reliable peak). Default 3 (0 = off); keeps ~98% of real-quality peaks. The companion to --mbr-min-snr. |

## `riana fit`

Fit kinetic models to a labeling time series (heavy water or ¹⁸O water).

Solves each peptidoform's fraction of new protein (θ) at every timepoint from its isotopomer envelope, then fits a kinetic model for its turnover rate k. With --manifest, runs are grouped into curves by (experiment, condition). Writes riana_fit_peptides.txt and riana_fit_fractions.txt.

```
riana fit [OPTIONS] [RIANA_PATH ...]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RIANA_PATH` | `FILE …` | Integrate output _riana.txt files (legacy/single-curve path; the sample field encodes the time point, e.g. time0, time6). Omit when using --manifest. |

### Options

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--manifest` | `FILE` | – | riana_manifest.tsv from `integrate --sdrf` (the primary path). Runs are grouped into kinetic curves by (experiment, condition) with the timepoint taken from the SDRF identity, not the filename. |
| `--coefficients` | `TEXT` | – | Labeling-site coefficient table — REQUIRED; the format depends on --label. hw: a per-AA D2O table (preset deberneh_2025_rss [recommended] \| ilchenko_2019 \| commerford_1983 \| alamillo_2025_{ac16,ipsc,cm}, or an (amino_acid, coefficient) CSV). o18: a length-model table (preset juber_2026_o18_ac16 [in-vitro] \| rachdaoui_2009_o18 [in-vivo mouse], or a (feature, coefficient) CSV). |
| `-m`, `--model` | `TEXT` | `simple` | Kinetic model: simple (default), guan, fornasiero. Or 'calibration' — a through-origin FS-vs-mixing-proportion recovery line (R² = recovery quality); auto-selected on --manifest calibration runs. |
| `-l`, `--label` | `TEXT` | `hw` | Labeling chemistry: 'hw' (heavy water / D2O, default) or 'o18' (metabolic H2-18O; length-model Spep + 3-isotope-O envelope). Each needs its matching --coefficients table. (Amino-acid / SILAC fitting was dropped — integrate SILAC peaks, fit L/(H+L) downstream.) |
| `--kp` | `FLOAT` | `0.5` | Precursor rate constant (two-compartment models). |
| `--kr` | `FLOAT` | `0.05` | Reutilization rate constant (Fornasiero). |
| `--rp` | `FLOAT` | `10.0` | Bound/free precursor ratio (Fornasiero). |
| `-q`, `--q_value` | `FDR` | `0.01` | Fit only data points with q-value below this [default: 1e-2]. |
| `-d`, `--depth` | `INTEGER` | `3` | Fit only peptidoforms seen at this many distinct labeling timepoints (per condition) [default: 3]. Counts distinct timepoints, not raw PSM rows — repeats at one timepoint don't count toward depth. |
| `-r`, `--ria` | `FLOAT` | – | Precursor enrichment (asymptotic labeled fraction, e.g. 0.06 for 6% v/v). Default: per-experiment from the manifest's precursor_enrichment (the SDRF value); given here, it overrides that for every curve. The legacy non-manifest path falls back to 0.06. |
| `-o`, `--out` | `PATH` | `.` | Output directory [default: .]. |
| `-f`, `--fs` | `N|AUTO` | – | Limited-isotopomer scoring: fit the FS on the leading channels iso0..isoN (give a single index N, e.g. '3' = iso0-iso3) to dodge co-eluting contaminants in the higher channels — integrate wide, fit narrow. Or 'auto': per-peptide width keyed on the natural-abundance envelope (iso0-3 for typical peptides, wider for broad ones; RIA-invariant). Default: score the full envelope. |
| `-W`, `--workers` | `N` | `1` | Worker *processes* for the per-peptide fit [default: 1]. The parallelism lever: dispatches over a process pool to sidestep the GIL (the per-peptide fit is GIL-bound). Results are identical regardless of N (per-peptide deterministic seed). |
| `--exclude-mbr` | flag | off | Drop match-between-runs data points (evidence='mbr') before fitting. MBR points are used by default; use this to compare with and without MBR. The n_mbr / n_clean output columns report the split either way. |
| `--min-spep` | `N` | – | Curation floor on a peptidoform's labelling-site count (Spep): drop those below N before fitting, so under-powered curves (too few sites for the envelope to shift measurably) never reach the results or rollup. Default is label-aware (8 for hw/D2O, 6 for o18 — o18's +2 Da/site shifts more per site); 0 disables. Tune up for short time series / slow turnover. |
| `--fraction-collapse` | `SUM|ANCHOR` | `sum` | How to combine LC fractions / technical replicates of one (peptidoform, charge, biorep, timepoint) before fitting (manifest path; SDRF comment[fraction identifier] defines the fractions). 'sum' (default): sum each isoN channel across fractions and intensity-weight the mass/QC columns. 'anchor': keep only the highest-total-intensity fraction (legacy parity). Intensities are always combined before a single FS is solved — fraction FS values are never averaged. |
| `--fs-rail-drop`, `--no-fs-rail-drop` | flag | on | Drop per-timepoint FS points beyond a 0.05 margin of the physical [0,1] range (over-labelled ≥1.05 or below-natural ≤−0.05) before counting fit points / depth — such a point is a failed solve, not a real measurement. On by default for all fits (margins chosen by benchmark); --no-fs-rail-drop reproduces the pre-1.2.0 numbers (rail-hits then fall to the R² gate). |

## `riana rollup`

Roll per-peptide fits up to protein turnover.

Per (experiment, condition, protein): collapses the peptides' θ within each biological replicate and timepoint (inverse-variance weighted) and refits k; the median of the peptides' k is reported alongside. With --model "linear simple" it also tests the turnover difference between two conditions (Δk), and with --interaction whether that difference varies between experiments. Reads the `riana fit` outputs from FIT_DIR or via --manifest and writes riana_rollup_proteins.txt and riana_rollup_fractions.txt.

```
riana rollup [OPTIONS] [FIT_DIR]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FIT_DIR` | `DIRECTORY` | Directory holding riana_fit_peptides.txt + riana_fit_fractions.txt from `riana fit`. Omit when using --manifest. |

### Options

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--manifest` | `FILE` | – | riana_manifest.tsv (the SDRF/project path). Finds the fit outputs from its stage='fit' rows and writes the rollup next to the manifest, recording stage='rollup' rows. With -o pointing elsewhere it forks a self-contained derived project there and leaves the input manifest untouched. |
| `-m`, `--model` | `TEXT` | `simple` | Kinetic model for the protein refit — match how the peptides were fit (simple, guan, fornasiero). Or 'linear simple': the linearized φ=log(1−θ) cross-sample model — fits a protein's conditions jointly for a per-condition k and a Δk test (writes delta_k / delta_k_p / delta_k_p_adj). Mutually exclusive with the ODE models. |
| `--phi-limit` | `PHI` | `-4.0` | ['linear simple' only] Plateau-truncation threshold in φ-space: points with φ=log(1−θ) at/below this are dropped per curve (saturated tail = measurement noise, not slope). −4 ≈ θ 0.98, −3 ≈ θ 0.95. |
| `--linear-weights` | `SCHEME` | `wls` | ['linear simple' only] Weighting of the φ-space fit: 'wls' (default) weights by the delta-method inverse variance (1−θ)², taken from the fitted value — φ=log(1−θ) makes FS-scale noise heteroscedastic, so an unweighted fit is anti-conservative (~28% false positives at α=0.05, and k biased ~14% low in the fast tail). 'wls-var' (opt-in) additionally weights by the per-point precision 1/Var̂(θ) (eBayes-moderated, robust-fitFDist d0) — ~10% better biological-replicate consistency on rich multi-peptide time series, safe/neutral elsewhere; needs the collapse's theta_var (else falls back to wls). 'ols' restores the old unweighted fit (audit only). --interaction uses the same weights ('ols' there falls back to 'wls'). |
| `--reference-condition` | `COND` | – | ['linear simple' only] Baseline condition of the Δk contrast — delta_k = k(test) − k(reference). Default: alphabetically first. |
| `--test-condition` | `COND` | – | ['linear simple' only] Comparison condition of the Δk contrast (requires --reference-condition). Naming a pair contrasts exactly those two even when &gt;2 conditions are present — an interim for multi-group projects before full all-pairwise. NOTE: the joint fit still pools the residual variance over ALL conditions in the data, so scope the SDRF conditions to the ones you mean to compare. |
| `--method` | `TEXT` | `weighted` | Protein estimator. 'weighted' (default): biorep-aware per-timepoint inverse-variance collapse, then one refit (pseudoreplication-safe). 'pooled': fit all peptide×timepoint points directly (pseudoreplication; for comparison). The median of peptide k is always carried as peptide_median_k for reference. |
| `--parsimony` | `TEXT` | `unique` | Protein attribution at summarize time. 'unique' (default): only single-accession peptides contribute (a shared peptide's envelope blends both proteins' turnover, so it can't be attributed). 'isoform': also fold isoform-only-shared peptides into the canonical entry, unless an isoform in the group carries its own unique peptide. |
| `--kp` | `FLOAT` | `0.5` | Precursor rate constant (two-compartment models). |
| `--kr` | `FLOAT` | `0.05` | Reutilization rate constant (Fornasiero). |
| `--rp` | `FLOAT` | `10.0` | Bound/free precursor ratio (Fornasiero). |
| `--min-peptides` | `INTEGER` | `2` | Min attributed peptides for a protein to be reported [default: 2]. |
| `--min-points` | `INTEGER` | `3` | Min collapsed (t, theta) points for the refit [default: 3]. |
| `--min-fit-points` | `N` | – | Peptide-level biological-replicate gate: keep only peptidoforms fit on &gt;= N points. Default auto = 2 for a SINGLE-TIMEPOINT experiment (detected from one distinct labeling time — R² is degenerate there, so curation rides on this replicate floor + --k-cv, with R²/rescue bypassed), off otherwise. Set 3+ to require more replicates, or 1 to disable. |
| `--peptide-admission` | `POLICY` | `auto` | How a peptide's per-condition curation result maps across conditions in a MULTI-condition rollup (single-condition is unaffected). 'auto' (default) → 'all' for `--model "linear simple"` (the Δk path, where a different-peptides-per-condition contrast is a real confound) and 'own' for the kinetic models. 'own': strictly per-condition — each condition's k / Δk term uses only peptides that pass the gate THERE. 'any': passed-in-one ⇒ kept-in-all (anti-conservative; the pre-2026-08 behaviour). 'all': kept only if it passes in EVERY condition it appears in (paired / common-support — the cleanest Δk basis, same peptides both sides, at the cost of yield). |
| `--min-spep` | `N` | – | Optional Spep (labelling-site) admission gate before rollup — drop peptides below N. Off by default (the primary gate is at `fit`, so a manifest rollup already inherits it); set this for explicit-file inputs or belt-and-braces. |
| `--min-r2` | `R2` | `0.8` | Peptide R² admission gate before rollup (default 0.8). Keep a peptide if R² ≥ this, OR (flat-curve rescue) R² ≥ --rescue-r2 and k_cv &lt; --k-cv. The gate is needed for good within-protein geom-CV (the inverse-variance weighting alone under-curates). Pass 0 (or any value ≤ 0) to disable it entirely. |
| `--k-cv` | `FLOAT` | `0.2` | Flat-curve rescue: max relative uncertainty of k̂ — k_cv = (ci_hi−ci_lo)/(2·\|k\|), a scale-free CV of the rate constant — for a low-R² peptide to still be admitted (only with --min-r2). Being scale-free it needs no retuning across time-series ranges or k units (/day vs /h), unlike an absolute SE. Set ≤ 0 to disable (R²-only gate). |
| `--rescue-r2` | `FLOAT` | `0.6` | Flat-curve rescue: min R² floor for the --k-cv rescue (only with --min-r2). Guards against degenerate k≈0 fits whose CI collapses to a spuriously tight k_cv; the exact value barely matters (any floor above the negative-R² band works), 0.6 is validated. |
| `-W`, `--workers` | `N` | `1` | Worker *processes* for the per-protein refit [default: 1]. The parallelism lever for the GIL-bound rollup: dispatches proteins over a process pool. Results are identical regardless of N (per-protein deterministic seed). |
| `--exclude-mbr` | flag | off | Drop match-between-runs fraction points (evidence='mbr') before the protein refit. MBR points are used by default; the n_mbr / n_clean output columns report the composition either way. |
| `--experiment` | `EXP` | – | Restrict the rollup to a single experiment (e.g. one tissue when the manifest was stratified via `integrate --experiment-column`). Default: all experiments in one pass, each contributing per-experiment rows to the one output table (Δk is always within-experiment). |
| `--plot` | flag | off | ['linear simple' only] Also write per-protein φ-space Δk comparison curves to a PDF per experiment (riana_rollup_curves[_&lt;exp&gt;].pdf) — the batch analog of the GUI's one-at-a-time view. One page per protein, sorted by delta_k_p_adj. |
| `--interaction` | flag | off | ['linear simple', 2+ experiments] Also test whether the condition effect differs between experiments that are strata of the SAME animals (e.g. tissues split with `integrate --experiment-column`). One joint fit per protein with a random slope per animal. The animal is the SDRF's characteristics[individual] when present; otherwise condition × labeling time × biological replicate, so biological_replicate must then identify the same animal in every experiment. Writes riana_rollup_interaction.txt: per-experiment k and Δk from the joint fit, the interaction test on the ratio scale (k_test/k_reference; primary) and on the additive scale, and the mean Δk across experiments, each BH-adjusted across proteins. Compares --reference-condition with --test-condition (or the other condition when there are exactly two). |
| `-o`, `--out` | `PATH` | `.` | Output directory [default: .]. |

## `riana gui`

Launch the desktop app (needs the optional gui extra: pip install "riana[gui]").

Integrate, Model (fit) and Protein (rollup) tabs over the same engine as the command line, with interactive chromatogram, curve and φ-space plots.

```
riana gui [OPTIONS]
```
